identification.summary: Long-running cyber-espionage actor tracked as Inception / Inception Framework (Blue Coat, Symantec, Palo Alto Networks Unit 42) and Cloud Atlas (Kaspersky, Check Point, F.A.C.C.T., Positive Technologies) [S1][S2][S4][S5]. It relies on spear-phishing with weaponized Office documents, layered script-based implants and command and control over legitimate cloud services [S1][S3][S5]. In December 2014 Kaspersky assessed that Cloud Atlas represents a rebirth of the RedOctober operation that it exposed in 2013 [S4]. Check Point reported that after February 2022 its targeting narrowed to Russia, Belarus and conflict-affected parts of Ukraine and Moldova [S2], and Kaspersky reported that more than 80% of 2024 VBCloud targets were in Russia [S3].
identification.firstObserved: Active since at least 2014 per Unit 42 [S1] and Symantec, as reported by Security Affairs (since at least May 2014) [S6]. Kaspersky saw the first Cloud Atlas attacks in August 2014 and links the actor to RedOctober, which it exposed in 2013 [S4].
identification.notes: No Microsoft name was identified for this actor in the sources gathered. Brandefense lists the aliases Inception Framework, Blue Odin, Cloud Atlas, Clean Ursa, ATK116, G0100 and OXYGEN [S9]. MITRE tracks it as Inception (G0100) [S10]. Kaspersky's RedOctober link rests on a shared compression method, compiler setup and overlapping targets in Russia, Kazakhstan and Belarus. It is a vendor assessment, not proof of the same operator [S4]. Palo Alto Networks noted in 2014 that both the Inception and Cloud Atlas campaigns used CloudMe for command and control [S5]. Sources disagree on whether Blue Coat or Symantec coined the name 'Inception Framework' [S9].

attribution.confidence: No sponsor was identified in the open sources gathered. The Record's coverage of F.A.C.C.T.'s December 2023 reporting describes the group as state-backed but names no sponsoring country [S7]. Security Affairs, reporting on Symantec and Akamai research, describes Inception as nation-state-backed without naming the state [S6]. No government attribution was found.
attribution.basis: Vendor reporting covers tradecraft and targeting but names no sponsoring state [S1][S2][S7]. Since 2022 the targeting has centred on Russia and Belarus [S2][S3]. Kaspersky's RedOctober lineage assessment rests on code and target overlap [S4].

objectives: Strategic intelligence collection against government, diplomatic and strategic-industry targets [S4][S5][S9]. The tooling is built for reconnaissance, system profiling and document theft [S1][S3]. Brandefense characterizes the goal as collection of diplomatic communications, government documents and related research [S9].

sectors: Executives in oil, finance and engineering; military officers; government officials [S5][S9]
Agro-industrial enterprises and state-owned research organizations [S7]
Defense sector (Russia, 2025, per Positive Technologies coverage) [S8]
Energy, defense, aerospace, research and media organizations [S9]
regions: Russia-controlled or contested areas of Ukraine and Moldova (2022) [S2]
Smaller 2024 VBCloud victim sets in Belarus, Canada, Moldova, Israel, Kyrgyzstan, Turkey and Vietnam [S3]
Africa, Europe and the Middle East (Brandefense profile) [S9]
targeting.notes: The 2014 lures referenced diplomatic car sales [S4]. Unit 42 saw the group in 2017 against government targets in Europe, Russia and Central Asia [S1]. Check Point says the post-2022 shift narrowed its scope but did not change its tactics [S2]. The 2023 lures appealed for support to Russian soldiers in the 'special military operation' [S7]. The cross-regional sector list comes from secondary profiles and is not tied to dated campaigns [S9].

capabilities.summary: Initial access is spear-phishing with Word documents. Kaspersky saw a CVE-2012-0158 variant in 2014 [S4]. Later campaigns used remote-template retrieval with Equation Editor exploits CVE-2017-11882 and CVE-2018-0802 [S1][S3][S7]. In 2014 the documents dropped a Visual Basic script that installed the loader and payload rather than writing a PE backdoor to disk [S4]. Command and control ran over CloudMe WebDAV storage [S5]. In 2018 Symantec reported that the group hid its origin behind chains of hijacked UPnP home routers, which needed no custom malware on the routers [S6]. In 2018 Unit 42 named POWERSHOWER, a PowerShell reconnaissance backdoor that cleans up after itself [S1]. Check Point reported a DLL in 2022 that proxies connections through victim machines [S2]. Kaspersky's 2024 reporting describes an HTA-to-VBShower chain that deploys PowerShower (network probing and payload download) and VBCloud (system information and file theft) [S3]. In 2025 Positive Technologies observed several new TLS certificates issued in a single day for fresh infrastructure [S8].

campaigns.name: RedOctober (precursor per Kaspersky)
campaigns.summary: Kaspersky exposed RedOctober, an espionage operation against embassies, after which its C2 network was dismantled. Kaspersky later assessed Cloud Atlas to be its rebirth.

campaigns.name: Cloud Atlas / Inception Framework disclosure
campaigns.summary: Kaspersky saw CVE-2012-0158 lures on diplomatic car-sale themes against Russia, Kazakhstan and Belarus. Blue Coat disclosed the layered Inception Framework using CloudMe WebDAV for C2.

campaigns.name: UPnP router proxy chaining
campaigns.summary: Symantec reported the group routing traffic through chains of hijacked UPnP routers. Akamai's UPnProxy research described a related 65,000-router proxy botnet.

campaigns.name: POWERSHOWER campaign against Europe
campaigns.summary: Unit 42 observed remote-template Word documents exploiting CVE-2017-11882 (and CVE-2012-1856) that delivered the new POWERSHOWER backdoor.

campaigns.name: Wartime targeting of Russia and Belarus
campaigns.summary: Check Point reported focused targeting of Russia, Belarus and conflict-affected areas of Ukraine and Moldova, plus a new DLL that proxies traffic through victims.

campaigns.name: War-themed lures against Russian organizations
campaigns.summary: F.A.C.C.T. reported blocked attacks on a Russian agro-industrial enterprise and a state-owned research company using lures about supporting soldiers.

campaigns.name: VBCloud campaign
campaigns.summary: Kaspersky documented VBCloud used against several dozen users in 2024, more than 80% of them in Russia, alongside VBShower and PowerShower.

campaigns.name: Defense-sector activity and new infrastructure
campaigns.summary: Positive Technologies reported Cloud Atlas activity against the Russian defense sector and several new TLS certificates issued in one day in February 2025.

diamond.adversary: Unattributed espionage actor tracked as Inception / Cloud Atlas since 2014. Kaspersky assesses lineage from RedOctober [S1][S4][S7].
diamond.capability: Weaponized Office documents using remote templates and Equation Editor exploits; VBS/HTA loaders; the VBShower, PowerShower/POWERSHOWER and VBCloud implants; a victim-side proxy DLL [S1][S2][S3][S4].
diamond.infrastructure: Cloud storage used for C2 (CloudMe WebDAV) [S5]; chains of hijacked UPnP home routers used as proxies [S6]; regularly refreshed domains and TLS certificates [S8].
diamond.victim: Diplomatic, government, defense, research and agro-industrial organizations, now mainly in Russia and Belarus [S2][S3][S4][S7][S8].
diamond.socioPolitical: Targeting narrowed to Russia, Belarus and contested areas of Ukraine and Moldova after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, which suggests intelligence requirements tied to that conflict [S2]. No sponsoring state is named [S7].
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints running Microsoft Office with unpatched Equation Editor; consumer routers exposing UPnP; legitimate cloud storage services [S1][S3][S5][S6].

gaps: No sponsoring state is named in open sources. Neither a government attribution nor a Microsoft name was found.

The primary Kaspersky Securelist reports could not be opened: securelist.com was blocked by the session proxy. Details of the VBCloud report and of the 2025 to early-2026 reports (including the PowerCloud tool) rest on search summaries and secondary coverage.
The original Blue Coat (2014), Symantec (2018) and F.A.C.C.T. (2023) reports were not opened. They are cited through secondary coverage.
Positive Technologies research (2024-2025) on Google Sheets C2 and Yandex.Disk-hosted modules was seen only in Russian-language summaries and has no confirmed date. It is not included as a campaign.
The Akamai 65,000-router UPnProxy botnet is only 'related' to Inception per coverage. Do not attribute the whole botnet to this actor.
Kaspersky's Cloud Atlas-RedOctober linkage and the merging of the Inception and Cloud Atlas vendor clusters are vendor assessments.
Brandefense's sector and region list (Africa, Middle East, aerospace, media) is not tied to dated primary campaign reporting.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: The operational environment includes diplomatic, government and defense networks and the cloud-storage and consumer-router infrastructure that the actor abuses for C2 and anonymization [S1][S5][S6]. STEP 2: Legacy Office Equation Editor flaws (CVE-2017-11882, CVE-2018-0802) remain usable years after patching. This shows that unpatched Office clients are the decisive terrain [S1][S3]. STEP 3: The doctrinal template runs from a themed spear-phish to a remote template or Equation Editor exploit, then an HTA/VBS loader (VBShower), then PowerShell reconnaissance (PowerShower), then file theft (VBCloud) over cloud or proxied C2 [S1][S3][S6]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued espionage against Russian and Belarusian government, defense and research targets; US and allied equities face spillover risk through the smaller victim sets in other countries [S2][S3][S8]. MDCOA is retasking against diplomatic or coalition entities with geopolitical lures, using residential-router proxy chains to frustrate attribution and blocking [S4][S6]. Candidate indicators: Word documents that fetch remote templates over HTTP; EQNEDT32 spawning mshta or wscript; VBS files with randomized names in user profile directories; outbound WebDAV to cloud storage; PowerShell reconnaissance followed by self-cleanup [S1][S3][S5].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: the current focus is on Russia and Belarus [S2][S3], so this actor is lower priority for DoDIN defense. Track it for retargeting signs, such as lures themed on coalition or diplomatic issues [S4]. (2) Authorities: no sponsoring state is named [S7], so any response beyond network defense needs careful attribution coordination; do not treat vendor lineage claims as government attribution [S4]. (3) Mission assurance: verify that Equation Editor is removed or disabled and that remote-template loading is restricted on mission systems, since the actor reuses years-old exploits [S1][S3]. (4) Coordination: its anonymization relies on consumer UPnP routers and legitimate cloud storage [S5][S6], so takedown or blocking requires coordination with cloud providers and partners rather than simple IP blocking.
